question: A membership team must recommend one new member benefit to its board. Which sequence of task types should they work through?
options: A) Write the recommendation; generate candidate benefits; look up what comparable bodies offer; weigh the shortlist against their budget.
B) Look up what comparable bodies offer; write the recommendation; weigh the shortlist against their budget; generate candidate benefits.
C) Generate candidate benefits; look up what comparable bodies offer; weigh the shortlist against their budget; write the recommendation.
D) Weigh the shortlist against their budget; write the recommendation; generate candidate benefits; look up what comparable bodies offer.
correct_answers: C) Generate candidate benefits; look up what comparable bodies offer; weigh the shortlist against their budget; write the recommendation.
explanations: Writing the recommendation first fixes the conclusion, and the generation and research stages then serve to justify a choice already made.
Research before generation is defensible, but the recommendation is written second here, ahead of the weighing and the generation it depends on.

Correct. Each task type feeds the next: open generation widens the field, research grounds the candidates in what others actually do, weighing against the budget narrows them, and only then is there a decision worth writing up.
A shortlist cannot be weighed before any candidates have been generated, so this ordering starts from something that does not yet exist.
